find: In the UK, copyright in a photograph, film or written work typically lasts for the creator's lifetime plus 70 years. After this period, the work enters the public domain and can be used freely.
replace: In the UK, copyright in written and artistic works, including photographs, usually lasts for 70 years after the creator dies. Film copyright lasts for 70 years after the last surviving director, screenplay author or composer dies.
note: F1: Film copyright is not tied to one creator.

expect: Copyright in a photograph, film or written work in the UK typically lasts for the creator's lifetime plus _____ years.
value: Copyright in a photograph or written work in the UK typically lasts for the creator's lifetime plus _____ years.
note: F1: The answer remains 70, but film has different term rules.

expect: When does copyright in a UK creative work typically expire?
value: When does copyright in a UK written or artistic work typically expire?
note: F1: The existing answer is valid only for written and artistic works.

find: Like PEGI 12+ ratings, BBFC 12A/12, 15 and 18 certificates carry legal force for cinema admissions.
replace: In cinemas, the age restrictions are 12A, 15 and 18; 12 applies to home entertainment releases.
note: F2: BBFC 12 is not a cinema classification.

find: PEGI 12, 16 and 18 ratings are legally enforceable in UK retail; BBFC 12A/12, 15 and 18 certificates are legally enforced for cinema admission.
replace: PEGI 12, 16 and 18 ratings are legally enforceable in UK retail. In cinemas, the age restrictions are 12A, 15 and 18; 12 applies to home entertainment releases.
note: F2: BBFC 12 is not a cinema classification.

find: Both systems have legally enforceable elements: PEGI 12, 16 and 18 are enforceable at UK retail points of sale; BBFC 12A/12, 15 and 18 certificates are enforced at UK cinemas.
replace: Both systems have legally enforceable elements: PEGI 12, 16 and 18 are enforced at UK retail points of sale; at cinemas, age restrictions apply to BBFC 12A, 15 and 18.
note: F2: BBFC 12 is for home entertainment releases.

find: PEGI rates video games (3, 7, 12, 16, 18) and the BBFC rates films (U, PG, 12A/12, 15, 18); PEGI 12, 16 and 18 and BBFC 12A/12, 15 and 18 are legally enforced, while lower categories are advisory.
replace: PEGI rates video games (3, 7, 12, 16, 18) and the BBFC classifies films and video works (U, PG, 12A/12, 15, 18). PEGI 12, 16 and 18 are legally enforced at UK retail; in cinemas, age restrictions apply to 12A, 15 and 18.
note: F2: BBFC 12 applies to home entertainment rather than cinema admission.

find: Media creators working with children must also ensure parental consent is obtained before recording or publishing any content featuring under-18s.
replace: When working with children, media creators should identify the appropriate lawful basis and follow their organisation's safeguarding procedures before recording or publishing identifiable content.
note: F3: Consent is not the only lawful basis for processing personal data.

find: When submitting coursework for this unit, students must produce pre-production documents including visualisation diagrams as evidence of planning before they begin creating their final product.
replace: For R093, you need to understand how visualisation diagrams support planning and judge their usefulness; you are not asked to make one from scratch.
note: F4: R093 is an exam and excludes creating planning documents from scratch.
